text: Agile methodology is a popular approach to project management, especially in software development. Instead of working on a project all at once, teams use an iterative process, breaking the work into small, manageable parts called sprints, which usually last one to four weeks. Each sprint begins by selecting tasks from a prioritized list known as a backlog. These tasks are often written as user stories, which describe a feature from the end user's perspective. To keep everyone aligned, the team holds a short daily meeting called a standup, where each member shares what they did yesterday, what they'll do today, and any obstacles they face. This cycle repeats, allowing for regular feedback and continuous improvement.
